summary: Prove lookup-not-constraint end to end, not just at the inventory store (TKT-235 ai-review)
description:
**Surfaced by TKT-235's ai-review (`gpt-5.6-luna`), finding 5 [medium].** Not a defect that ticket
introduced — a gap between what its tests prove and what its design *claims*.

TKT-235 established the sales-channel registry as a **lookup, not a constraint**: an unregistered —
or disabled — channel code must sell exactly as it did before the registry existed. Two tests guard
it, and both are narrower than the claim:

- `services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go` →
  `TestAnUnregisteredChannelCodeStillSells` calls the **inventory store directly**. It never
  traverses commerce orchestration, catalog fee resolution, split resolution, payments, or any API
  boundary. A registry lookup added at any of those layers would reject the sale *earlier* and leave
  this test green.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/channels_smoke_test.go` → `TestNothingReferencesTheChannelRegistry`
  greps `information_schema` for foreign keys pointing at `channels`. That proves **FK absence in
  catalog's schema**. It says nothing about application-level gating anywhere.

Both had their scope narrowed in comments at review time, so nothing currently overclaims in the
code. What is missing is the test that would actually catch the regression.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A gateway-level (or `smoke/`) test buys through the full path — reserve → fee resolution → split
  resolution → confirm — using a channel code that has **no registry row at all**, and asserts the
  sale completes with the code recorded verbatim on the claim and the order.
- The same path with a channel code whose registry row exists but is **`enabled = false`**, and it
  also completes. Disabling is a *display* decision (it removes the channel from
  `/public/channels`), not a sellability one — nothing in the sale path consults the registry today,
  and this test is what stops that changing silently.
- Both assertions name the invariant and cite ADR-024, so a future ticket that deliberately adds
  registry gating has to change the test and state why, rather than deleting it.

Quality gates: `make check` green. Test-only ticket — if it surfaces a real gating bug in the sale
path, report it and stop rather than fixing it here.

Parent: TKT-17. Non-goals: adding any registry enforcement (that would be the opposite of this
ticket); the seated-pool seam (TKT-176).

governingAdrs.why: The load-bearing decision. The no-FK rule (historical attribution must survive a channel being retired) is what makes 'lookup, not constraint' true. RE-RESOLVED at claim: amended by TKT-246 (allocations may bind a seller via sold_by) and TKT-250 (allocation set carries a revision) since this memo was first captured. Both amendments are guards on channel_allocations, NOT on catalog.channels -- the distinction this test exists to pin.

Fee resolution takes a channel and is one of the layers the end-to-end test must traverse. A registry lookup added here would reject the sale before inventory is ever reached, leaving the inventory-store test green.

Split resolution is channel-selective and is the other such layer. Note it is NOT a separate HTTP call -- splits ride inside the fee-resolution response and are persisted in fee_resolution_snapshot, so traversing fee resolution traverses both.

ADDED at shaping (absent from the 2026-08-09 capture). Per-channel sales windows are the FIRST predicate in the inventory claim guard (window -> seller -> code -> capacity). It gates on channel_allocations, not the registry, but it is a channel-keyed refusal the fixture must not trip, or the test never reaches the INSERT it means to assert on.

governingTests.name: services/commerce/internal/api/channel_seam_test.go
governingTests.why: A LIVE TRIPWIRE, not background. It pins the public reserve route as channel-free until the seam closes, and its header says 'when TKT-246 lands these assertions INVERT; do not delete them' -- then records that they did NOT invert. Any change that makes the public route forward a channel fails here. This ticket must not touch it.

governingTests.name: smoke/coverage_test.go
governingTests.why: Every documented 2xx operation of inventory/commerce/payments/access must be driven by some smoke test, enforced in TestMain. A new smoke file adds coverage, never removes it, but the gate runs on every make check.

governingTests.name: services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:470-497
governingTests.why: The existing test's own scope disclaimer names TKT-241 as the owner of the gateway-level version. Its wording is the charter; the new test should be reachable from it.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Filed from TKT-235 ai-review — incidental, deferred

**Finding:** [medium] *"The lookup-not-constraint regression test does not exercise a sale
boundary"* — `gpt-5.6-luna`, TKT-235 ai-review pass 1.

**Triage: incidental, not blocking.** The reviewer is right that the test is narrower than the
claim, and wrong that this makes the claim false today: nothing in the sale path reads the registry
at all (verified — no reference to `channels` or `ListEnabledChannels` anywhere in commerce or
inventory outside generated types). So there is **no defect in the diff**; there is a missing guard
against a defect a *future* ticket could introduce. Building a full gateway-level purchase harness
is its own vertical slice, well beyond a registry story's scope.

**Done at review time instead:** both tests had their scope narrowed in their own comments, so
neither overclaims in the code. This ticket carries the real coverage.

Needs shaping before Gate 1 — the 8-item DoR is not filled and `first_slice` in particular needs a
decision on whether this rides `smoke/` or the gateway suite.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Shaping pass — 2026-08-16. Verdict: **all 8 items `met`, no open blockers → Gate 1 clears.**

Ran per `references/shaping.md`: read the real code first, then Example-Mapped what was left.
Nothing needed a spike and nothing needs a human decision. Detail is on the `readiness` field;
the four things a reader should not have to diff for:

**1. The COS as filed is partly unachievable, and that is by design — not a bug to fix here.**

The ticket asks for the channel code "recorded verbatim on the claim *and* the order" from a
single full-path purchase. It cannot be, because the **public** route deliberately forwards no
channel to inventory (`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:363-381`). TKT-240 added that
forward and it was **reverted** after its own adversarial review — `POST /reservations` is
unauthenticated and takes `channel_code` from the body, so forwarding alone let any caller drain
a reseller's allocation with no credential. TKT-246 then closed the seam only where a channel can
be *authorized* (the partner route, channel from the credential) and kept the public route unable
to reach the decision at all. `channel_seam_test.go:13-58` is a live tripwire pinning exactly
this, with instructions not to delete it.

So `claims.channel_code` is **NULL by design** on a public sale. The ticket text predates TKT-246
and did not know that.

**Correction, not deferral:** the test splits in two, each proving the invariant at the layer that
can actually carry it — **(A) public path** → assert `orders.channel_code` verbatim, having
traversed price + fee (ADR-046) + split (ADR-047) resolution, which are precisely the layers a
registry lookup would be added to; **(B) partner path** → assert `claims.channel_code` *and*
`orders.channel_code` verbatim. Between them the original COS is fully covered, and neither
overclaims. `first_slice` is decided: **`smoke/`**, because there is no separate "gateway suite" —
`smoke/` *is* the gateway-level tier and is already in `make check`.

**2. The invariant is sharper than the ticket words it, and the sharpening is the whole test.**

The claim path guards on **inventory's `channel_allocations`**, never on **catalog's `channels`**.
Two different tables in two different services. The guard is four ordered predicates
(`store.go:500-600`): `window → seller → code → capacity` — and *not one of them* consults the
registry. Writing the test as "a channel with no row sells" without saying *which table* is how it
would end up green and vacuous.

**Guard predicate count, per `shaping.md`:** the fixture must satisfy **all four** to reach the
`INSERT` it asserts on — active allocation for the code, open window, `sold_by` admitting the
caller (or unbound), `requires_code` false, cap ≥ qty. Trip any earlier predicate and the test
proves nothing about the registry while looking like it does. This is the failure mode
`docs/learnings/2026-08-10-a-green-test-that-cannot-reach-the-failing-state.md` names, and the one
the existing inventory test already dodged deliberately (`channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:496`).

**3. The stored context-mémo was stale and has been re-resolved.**

Captured 2026-08-09; since then **ADR-024 took two amendments** (TKT-246 `sold_by`, TKT-250
allocation revision) and **ADR-054** (per-channel sales windows) became the *first* predicate in
the claim guard — and was missing from `governingAdrs` entirely. Added, with the reason it matters
to *this* ticket (it is a channel-keyed refusal the fixture must not trip). All four cited ADRs
verified to resolve at HEAD. `governingTests` added and populated — `channel_seam_test.go` in
particular is a tripwire this ticket must not touch.

**4. Verified, not assumed: nothing on the sale path reads the registry today.**

Zero references to the `channels` table or `ListEnabledChannels` in commerce, inventory, payments
or the gateway; catalog only, plus generated UI types. So there is no gating bug to report — the
ticket's "if it surfaces a real gating bug, stop" branch does not trigger. The `enabled = false`
half is reachable directly at create time (`POST /api/catalog/channels` accepts `enabled`), no
update leg needed.

**`risk:low`: not claimed.** Test-only and touches no production code, which argues for it — but
the work is a *new end-to-end fixture across five services*, and the failure mode being guarded
against is a test that passes without proving anything. That is exactly the class the plan gate
catches. Running the plan gate.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — running gateless per `config.gates: autonomous`

**Gate 1 taken by the agent:** promoted `Backlog → Ready` on the shaping pass of **2026-08-16**,
per `config.gates: autonomous`. The promotion is earned by that pass, not by the ticket text —
which, as the readiness verdict records, was wrong about what its own COS could prove.

Condition checked before the transition, item by item (`shaping.md`: the board's drag-block does
not bind a POST, so the agent is the enforcement): all **8 readiness items `met`** — none `open`,
**none `deferred`**, no item carrying `owner: "human"`, **no open `blocked-by` link**, no spike
spawned or outstanding. The `approach: deferred` carve-out for auth / money / migrations /
CI-deploy config does not apply: `approach` is `met`, resolved by reading the code.

**No `deferred` items ⇒ nothing carried forward into `overrides:` from this gate.**

**Selection reason:** named directly by the owner ("run TKT-241"), so priority stays theirs —
selection was not the agent walking the backlog.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.** Stated explicitly rather than left silent, because this
is the ticket whose risk looks obvious to the claimer. The case *for* the label is real: test-only,
zero production code, an explicit non-goal of adding any registry enforcement. It is refused anyway
on two grounds:

1. The deliverable is a **new end-to-end fixture spanning five services** through the real compose
   stack — well past the "trivial and isolated" bar, and past the >5-files heuristic in spirit even
   if the file count lands lower.
2. The specific failure mode this ticket exists to prevent is **a test that is green without
   proving anything**. The claim guard has four ordered predicates (`window → seller → code →
   capacity`); a fixture that trips any of them early never reaches the `INSERT` it asserts on and
   is silently vacuous. A test-only ticket whose whole value is the test's *validity* is exactly
   what the plan gate is for. Skipping it here would be optimising the wrong risk.

Branch: `TKT-241-prove-lookup-not-constraint-end-to-end`. Next: `agent:planning`, drafted by
`config.models.plan` = `gpt-5.6-luna`.

### Plan draft — by `config.models.plan` = **`gpt-5.6-luna`** (codex `task`, read-only, effort high)

Drafted against the real code (the job's log shows it reading `store.go`, the orders schema, the
`smoke/` helpers, `channels.go` and `catalog/api/openapi.yaml`). Briefed from the ticket, the
re-resolved context-mémo, the four governing ADRs and the four governing tests. Verbatim below;
critique follows as `kind=plan-final`.

---

## Execution plan for TKT-241

### DoD

Create one new black-box smoke test file under `smoke/` that:

- Proves an unregistered public channel code completes a reservation and order.
- Proves the fixed partner channel completes when unregistered.
- Creates a disabled catalog channel and proves a public sale using that code still completes.
- Traverses catalog price, fee, and split resolution, commerce reservation orchestration, inventory, payments, and checkout.
- Asserts exact `channel_code` persistence in:
  - `commerce.reservations`
  - `commerce.orders`
  - `inventory.claims` for the partner path
- Makes no production changes.
- Leaves `channel_seam_test.go` untouched.
- Passes `make check`.

### Governing decisions

- ADR-024: inventory allocations and catalog registry are separate; no catalog FK or registry constraint may be introduced. Historical attribution must survive registry retirement.
- ADR-046: commerce must traverse catalog fee resolution using the submitted channel.
- ADR-047: split resolution is embedded in the fee-resolution response; no separate HTTP call is needed.
- ADR-054: any channel allocation fixture must have an open window, because window is the first inventory predicate.

The existing store test at [`channel_allocations_smoke_test.go`]( /home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:470) already names TKT-241 as the gateway-level owner. Do not modify it.

### Test structure

Use three top-level test functions, corresponding to the three independent scenarios:

1. `TestPublicSaleWithUnregisteredChannelCodeCompletes`
2. `TestPartnerSaleWithUnregisteredChannelCodeCompletes`
3. `TestPublicSaleWithDisabledChannelCodeCompletes`

Separate functions keep the public and partner authorization shapes independent and make failures diagnostic. The four inventory predicates are positive fixture preconditions here, not separate behaviors under test; adding four refusal tests would expand this ticket into guard testing.

#### 1. Public, unregistered code

Fixture:

- `publishedSlot(t, uniqueName, 20)`
- Quantity: `1`
- Fresh code such as `tkt241-public-<uuid>`
- Verify `catalog.channels` has no row for `(organizerID, code)`.
- Do not create an inventory allocation for this code.
- No `opens_at`/`closes_at`, `sold_by`, or `requires_code` apply because the public route sends no channel to inventory.
- Pool is published/open with capacity 20 and no existing claims.

The public route carries `channel_code` to catalog fee resolution and commerce persistence, then inventory receives an empty channel and takes the public-pool branch. Therefore no `channel_allocations` row is required.

Seed a channel-specific fee rule and split schedule directly in the catalog database for this unique code so the request exercises:

- catalog price resolution;
- catalog fee resolution;
- embedded split resolution;
- persistence of the fee-resolution snapshot.

Assertions:

- `POST /api/commerce/reservations` returns `201`.
- Reservation response has a reservation and hold ID.
- Fee breakdown contains the seeded fee code.
- Persisted fee snapshot contains the split result.
- `POST /api/commerce/orders` with `payment_token: "fake-ok"` returns `200` and `status: "completed"`.
- `commerce.reservations.channel_code == code`.
- `commerce.orders.channel_code == code`.

Red mutations:

- Add a catalog-registry existence/enabled check in fee resolution: reservation creation must fail.
- Remove `resolveTicketTypeFees`: fee breakdown/snapshot assertions fail.
- Remove `SelectSplitSchedule(...)` assignment in catalog fee resolution: split snapshot assertion fails.
- Remove `channel_code` from the reservation INSERT: reservation/order attribution fails.
- Remove `r.channel_code` from the checkout order INSERT at `server.go:1244`: the reservation remains correct but the order assertion fails.

#### 2. Partner, unregistered code

Use the existing credential-derived values:

- `partnerChannel()`, which is fixed at `reseller-smoke`.
- `partnerReseller()`.
- `partnerToken()`.

Before selling, query catalog directly and assert that `reseller-smoke` has no catalog registry row. The smoke script enrolls the partner but does not create a catalog channel, so this is the correct explicit verification.

Fixture:

- Fresh published slot with capacity 20.
- Inventory allocation via the existing internal PUT helper:
  - `channel`: `partnerChannel()`
  - `cap`: `4`
  - `sold_by`: `partnerReseller()`
  - omit `opens_at` and `closes_at` for an always-open window;
  - omit `requires_code`, which defaults false.
- Quantity: `1`.
- No prior consumption.

This satisfies all four predicates:

- window: always open;
- seller: credential reseller matches `sold_by`;
- code: no presale code required;
- capacity: cap 4 and pool capacity 20 exceed quantity 1.

Call `POST /api/commerce/partners/reservations`; the body must not contain `channel_code`. The credential supplies it.

Then confirm through `POST /api/commerce/orders`.

Assertions:

- Partner reservation returns `201`.
- Fee and split snapshot assertions match the public test.
- Checkout returns completed.
- `inventory.claims.channel_code == partnerChannel()`.
- `commerce.reservations.channel_code == partnerChannel()`.
- `commerce.orders.channel_code == partnerChannel()`.

Red mutations:

- Delete the credential-to-request assignment in `reserveWithScope` (`in.ChannelCode = &channel`): claim attribution becomes null.
- Delete the partner inventory body’s channel assignment around `server.go:543`: the claim assertion fails.
- Add a catalog registry existence/enabled check: the unregistered partner reservation fails.
- Remove `r.channel_code` from the checkout order INSERT: order attribution fails.

The partner code cannot be random: it is fixed by the enrolled credential. A fresh code would require creating a second credential and is outside this ticket.

#### 3. Public, disabled registry row

Fixture:

- Fresh published slot with capacity 20.
- Fresh random code such as `tkt241-disabled-<uuid>`.
- Create the registry row through:

  `postJSON(t, gatewayURL+"/api/catalog/channels", ...)`

  with:

  ```json
  {
    "code": "...",
    "display_name": "TKT-241 disabled",
    "kind": "reseller",
    "enabled": false
  }
  ```

  `postJSON` supplies the catalog staff-write credential and organizer assertion.
- Assert the create response says `enabled: false`.
- Seed the matching fee rule and split schedule.
- Do not create an inventory allocation; this remains a public-pool sale.
- Quantity: `1`.

Run the same public reservation and order flow.

Assertions:

- The catalog row is demonstrably disabled.
- Reservation completes.
- Fee/split resolution completes.
- Order completes.
- Reservation and order preserve the code verbatim.

Red mutations:

- Force `CreateChannel` to ignore the submitted `enabled:false`: the fixture assertion fails.
- Add an enabled-only registry gate to fee resolution: reservation creation fails.
- Remove order attribution persistence: the order DB assertion fails.

Do not assert `GET /public/channels` here. Its enabled-only behavior is already covered by catalog tests, and adding it would test storefront selector visibility rather than sale eligibility.

### Fresh versus `reseller-smoke`

Recommendation:

- Public scenarios: fresh random code per run. This provides explicit isolation and avoids stale catalog rows.
- Partner scenario: use `reseller-smoke`, because the channel is fixed by the credential and cannot be chosen by the request.

The partner test should fail clearly if a catalog row already exists for `reseller-smoke`; it must not silently reinterpret a disabled or registered row as “unregistered.” This assumes the normal smoke stack lifecycle starts with a clean catalog database. Do not delete existing rows from the test to force isolation.

### Database versus order API read

Use direct DB assertions.

`GET /api/commerce/orders/{id}` exposes only `order_id` and `status`; its `OrderState` contract does not expose `channel_code`. Therefore it cannot prove verbatim attribution.

Use the existing `dsn(role, database)` helper:

- `dsn("catalog", "catalog")` for registry fixture checks/seeding;
- `dsn("inventory", "inventory")` for `claims.channel_code`;
- `dsn("commerce", "commerce")` for reservation and order attribution.

### Files

Create only:

- [`smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go`]( /home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go) — new `//go:build smoke`, `package smoke_test` end-to-end coverage and small catalog/DB fixture helpers.

Do not modify:

- `services/commerce/internal/api/channel_seam_test.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go`
- `smoke/coverage_test.go`
- any production code, OpenAPI contract, generated file, script, or ADR.

The existing smoke coverage gate already runs all smoke tests without a `-run` allowlist, and the relevant commerce/inventory operations already have coverage drivers.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan critique + finalization — critique by `config.models.planReview` = **`main-agent`** (≠ `plan`, cross-model holds)

Adversarial pass over the `gpt-5.6-luna` draft. **Every file, symbol and seam the draft names was
verified to exist at HEAD** — `dsn(role, database)` (`smoke/smoke_test.go:57`, and roles
`catalog`/`inventory`/`commerce`/`payments` are all in live use), `postWithKey`
(`smoke/checkout_test.go:39`), `publishedSlot` (`smoke/operational_holds_test.go:114`),
`partnerChannel`/`partnerReseller`/`partnerDo`, `POST /api/catalog/channels` with a settable
`enabled`, and `fake-ok` as the PSP token. Nothing was hallucinated.

**Verdict: ACCEPT the draft's structure — three test functions, `smoke/`, direct DB assertions,
fresh codes for public / credential channel for partner — with the amendments below.**
The kind=plan draft as amended here is the plan.

---

#### AMENDMENT 1 — the public half must assert `claims.channel_code IS NULL`. [required]

The draft says the public route sends no channel to inventory and therefore needs no allocation.
**That is correct**, and I verified it rather than accepting it: `addSellerScope`
(`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:539-545`) returns early on `scope == nil`, so the public
hold body never gets a `channel` key at all.

But the draft reaches that conclusion by *reading*, and there is a live contradiction in the repo
that a future reader will hit: `smoke/checkout_test.go:906` says, in a public-route test with
`channel_code`, *"Both channels need an INVENTORY ALLOCATION, not only a fee rule (TKT-240)"*. That
comment describes the world during TKT-240's forward, which was reverted — its allocations are now
belt-and-braces. Two plausible readings of the same system, and `AGENTS.md` is explicit that a
claim like this is a hypothesis until it is executed.

**So make the test settle it.** The public half asserts, positively, that the claim row's
`channel_code` **IS NULL** while `reservations.channel_code` and `orders.channel_code` hold the code
verbatim. That single assertion (a) converts the draft's reasoning into an executed fact, (b) pins
the public/partner asymmetry that the whole two-function split rests on, and (c) becomes a second
tripwire beside `channel_seam_test.go` — at the DB tier, where the mechanism actually lives, rather
than one tier above it.

Without it the public half is compatible with a world where the channel *did* reach the claim, and
the reader cannot tell which world they are in.

#### AMENDMENT 2 — seed the fee rule, and say why it is load-bearing. [required]

The draft seeds a channel-specific fee rule and split schedule but does not justify it, which reads
like fixture ceremony that a later reader may trim. It is not ceremony, and the reason is sharper
than the draft states:

`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:805-808` — **"No rule matched is a successful resolution
with an empty fee set; it is not a failure and must never be conflated with one."**

So a sale with *no* fee rule completes **identically** whether fee resolution ran correctly, ran
degenerately, or was skipped. A test without a seeded rule traverses ADR-046/ADR-047 and observes
nothing — the exact vacuity this ticket exists to eliminate, reproduced inside the fix. The seeded
channel-scoped rule is what makes the traversal *observable*: a registry gate added to fee
resolution changes the fee outcome, and only a non-empty expected fee can see that.

**Therefore the assertion must be on the fee's VALUE, not on the sale's success** — assert the
resolved fee equals the seeded amount, and derive that expectation **from the seed** (300/ticket ×
qty), never from a first run. `AGENTS.md`: *a green test can assert the defect as correct* —
`TKT-239` pinned a number by observing what the code did. Write the number the rule says, then run.

Seeding is direct SQL into catalog (`dsn("catalog","catalog")`) — there is **no HTTP API for fee
rules**; `smoke/checkout_test.go:895-905` is the established precedent for exactly this INSERT.
`split_schedules` columns verified at
`services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0017_payees_and_split_schedules.sql:45-70`
(note: `channel_code` nullable, no `currency` column — shares are basis points).

#### AMENDMENT 3 — the partner half's "unregistered" precondition must be asserted, not assumed. [required]

The draft gets this right in instinct and I am hardening it into a rule, because it is the single
place this test could rot into a lie without anyone noticing.

The partner channel is `reseller-smoke`, fixed by the credential. It is unregistered **only because
`scripts/smoke.sh` happens never to create a catalog `channels` row** — an absence, and absences
drift. The moment some future ticket adds a registry row for `reseller-smoke` to the smoke
bootstrap, this test silently stops testing the unregistered case while staying green and
keeping its name.

**So: query `catalog.channels` for `(organizerID, 'reseller-smoke')` and `t.Fatal` if a row
exists**, with a message naming what broke and why (not `t.Skip` — a skip is how a suite silently
proves nothing; `smoke/partner_reserve_test.go:28-34` already sets this precedent by `t.Fatal`-ing
on absent credentials). **Do not delete the row to force isolation** — the draft is right, and the
reason is that deleting it would let the test manufacture the precondition it claims to observe,
which is the "repairing the precondition during setup" failure named in
`docs/learnings/2026-08-10-a-green-test-that-cannot-reach-the-failing-state.md`.

#### AMENDMENT 4 — mutation-check every assertion, and record the result. [required]

The draft's "red mutations" section is its strongest part and I am accepting it wholesale, with one
addition: it is not enough to *list* them. `AGENTS.md` and the Hard rules require the mutation to be
**executed** — break the mechanism, observe red, restore — and the result recorded in the stage
comment. The four predicates on the claim path mean an assertion can be refused for a reason
unrelated to the registry and still look green.

Minimum executed set (one per scenario, chosen to be the one that would actually rot):
1. Remove `r.channel_code` from the order INSERT (`server.go:1244`) → both order assertions red.
2. Delete `in.ChannelCode = &channel` in `reserveWithScope` (`server.go:630-635`) → partner claim
   assertion red.
3. Make the public route forward the channel to inventory (add `body["channel"]`) → **Amendment 1's
   `IS NULL` assertion goes red**, which is the proof that assertion is load-bearing and not
   decorative.

#### REJECTED from the draft — nothing.

No part of the draft was rejected. Two things it *declined* to do are explicitly endorsed:
- **Not asserting `GET /public/channels`** in the disabled case. Correct: that is storefront selector
  visibility, already covered by catalog's own tests, and conflating "disappears from the selector"
  with "cannot sell" is the exact category error this ticket refutes.
- **Not adding four refusal tests** for the four guard predicates. Correct *for this ticket*: here
  the predicates are fixture preconditions, not the behaviour under test. The `N predicates needs N
  tests` rule binds a ticket that *ships* a guard; this one ships a test that must get *past* one.
  Noted so a reviewer does not re-raise it.

---

### REQUIRED SECTION — introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Design elements **added** by this critique (not accepted/amended/rejected from the draft). These
reach Gate 2 reviewed by nobody but their author, and are named again here so the ai-review pass
attacks them specifically:

1. **The `claims.channel_code IS NULL` assertion on the public half** (Amendment 1) — entirely new;
   the draft asserted nothing about the claim on the public path.
2. **Asserting the fee's VALUE rather than the sale's success** (Amendment 2) — the draft seeded the
   rule but asserted only that the breakdown "contains the seeded fee code"; deriving an expected
   amount from the seed is my addition, and it is the assertion most likely to be wrong in detail

Both are test-side, so the blast radius is a red gate, not a production defect — but #2 in
particular is an assertion whose *expected value* I derived by reading, and if the response shape
differs the implementer must fix the expectation from the contract, **never by running it and
pasting what came back**.

No decision was left open by the draft — it answered all four explicit questions conclusively and I
verified each independently:

| Question | Decision | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh code or `reseller-smoke`? | **Both**: fresh per-run codes for the two public scenarios, `reseller-smoke` for the partner one | The partner channel is credential-fixed; there is no choice to make. Forced, not preferred. |

**One new file, no production changes:** `smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go`

| Test | Proves |
|---|---|
| `TestAPublicSaleOnAnUnregisteredChannelCompletesEndToEnd` | A code with no registry row sells through reserve → price/fee/split resolution → order; `orders.channel_code` verbatim; **and `claims.channel_code IS NULL`** |
| `TestAPartnerSaleOnAnUnregisteredChannelCompletesEndToEnd` | Same via the credentialled partner route; **`claims.channel_code`** *and* the order/reservation verbatim |

#### Two fixture bugs found by running, not by reading

1. **The split seed needed a payee and balanced parts.** `INSERT INTO split_schedules` alone fails
   with `split schedule % has no parts` — `0017_payees_and_split_schedules.sql` defers the balance
   check to COMMIT and rejects an empty header. Fixed with a single transaction: payee →
   schedule → one part at 10000 bps. This is why the first run was red, and it is a good example of
   the plan's `first_slice` being right and its fixture detail being incomplete.
2. **A gate run reported "No rule to make target"** — the TKT-71 shape, from a background shell not
   inheriting the repo cwd. Fixed by `make -C <abs path>`. The sentinel caught it; the harness
   reported that same run as "exit code 0" while `EXIT=2` was on disk, which is exactly the
   divergence the skill says to expect. **Every PASS/FAIL below is from the sentinel plus the log
   body, never the harness status.**

#### Mutation checks — executed, not listed (Amendment 4)

Each mutation applied to production code, full gate run, then restored. `git diff --quiet` verified
clean between every one.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `orders` INSERT stops copying `r.channel_code` (`server.go:1244`) | **RED** — public and disabled tests die on `orders.channel_code is NULL, want a channel code`. The partner test also dies, but *earlier*, on `orders_reseller_implies_channel` (a 500 at checkout) — so mutation 1 does **not** independently prove the partner test's order assertion. Recorded rather than glossed. |
| 2 | Drop `in.ChannelCode = &channel` in `reserveWithScope` | **RED, but at a lower tier** — `channel_seam_test.go`'s `TestAPartnerGASaleForwardsItsChannelAndReseller` fires first and the smoke tier never runs. Correct defence-in-depth; inconclusive for my assertion. |
| 3 | `claims` INSERT writes `NULL` instead of `NULLIF($11,'')` | **RED, also at a lower tier** — 15 inventory store tests fail first. Same verdict as #2. |
| 4 | **A registry lookup added to catalog's fee resolution** (`ResolveTicketTypeFees` refuses a code absent from `ListEnabledChannels`) | **RED — and this is the one that matters.** |

**Mutation 4 is the ticket's whole thesis, executed.** All three new tests fail at their own reserve
step (`502 catalog unavailable`), each with the message written for this case. And in the same run:

```
ok  ticketing/services/catalog/internal/store    35.110s
ok  ticketing/services/inventory/internal/store  33.472s
```

**Both existing guards stayed green** — `TestAnUnregisteredChannelCodeStillSells` and
`TestNothingReferencesTheChannelRegistry` did not notice a change that makes the registry
authoritative on the sale path. That is precisely the gap TKT-235's ai-review predicted and this
ticket was filed to close, now demonstrated rather than argued.

**Honest limitation:** mutations 2 and 3 are caught at a lower tier, so the partner test's
`claims.channel_code` assertion is **not** independently mutation-proven end to end — a lower-tier
test would fail first in any run where it could have caught something. I could not construct a
mutation that isolates it through the full gate without disabling other tiers, and disabling them
produced a broken harness rather than a clean experiment. The assertion is still worth having (it
pins the value at the tier that stores it), but I am not claiming mutation evidence for it. This is
flagged for the ai-review pass.

objective.note: TKT-235's 'the channel registry is a lookup, not a constraint' is guarded only by an inventory-store-level test and a catalog FK-absence test. Neither crosses a service boundary, so a registry lookup added in commerce, catalog fee/split resolution, or the gateway would reject a sale earlier and leave both green. This ticket buys the end-to-end guard.

scope.note: IN: new smoke/ test(s) (//go:build smoke, package smoke_test) driving the real docker-compose stack through the gateway. OUT: any registry enforcement (the opposite of this ticket); the seated-pool seam (TKT-176); closing the public-route fee-attribution seam (TKT-247).

uncertainties.note: Resolved by reading at shaping. (1) Nothing on the sale path reads catalog's channels registry: zero hits for ListEnabledChannels / channels-table access in commerce, inventory, payments and gateway; only catalog and generated UI types. (2) The inventory claim guard reads channel_allocations (inventory's OWN table), never catalog.channels -- the two are distinct and conflating them is the trap this test must not fall into. (3) No allowlist gating: scripts/smoke.sh:304 runs go test -tags smoke ./... with no -run, so a new file cannot silently never run.

dependencies.note: No blocked-by links, none needed. Depends only on infrastructure that already exists: scripts/smoke.sh's stack lifecycle, the SMOKE_PARTNER_TOKEN/CHANNEL/RESELLER_ID credentials it enrols (smoke.sh:260-274), and the publishedSlot / internalJSON / partnerDo / created helpers.

approach.note: VERIFIED AGAINST THE CODE, and it corrects the ticket text. The ticket's COS asks for the code 'recorded verbatim on the claim AND the order' from one path. That is not achievable from one path, and the reason is deliberate: the PUBLIC route POST /api/commerce/reservations forwards no channel to inventory at all (services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:363-381; TKT-240 forwarded it and was REVERTED because that route is unauthenticated; TKT-246 kept it closed). channel_seam_test.go:13-58 is a live tripwire pinning that. So claims.channel_code is NULL by design on a public sale. The test therefore splits in two, each proving the invariant at the layer that can carry it: (A) PUBLIC path -- unregistered channel_code in the body, reserve -> price/fee/split resolution -> order confirm; assert 2xx and orders.channel_code == the code verbatim. This traverses ADR-046 fee resolution and ADR-047 split resolution, the exact layers a registry lookup would be added to. (B) PARTNER path -- POST /api/commerce/partners/reservations under SMOKE_PARTNER_TOKEN, whose channel comes from the CREDENTIAL, then confirm via POST /api/commerce/orders; assert claims.channel_code AND orders.channel_code == the code. 'reseller-smoke' already has no catalog registry row (smoke.sh never creates one), which is the unregistered case for free. Template: smoke/partner_reserve_test.go:27-107 plus a confirm leg. GUARD PREDICATE COUNT on the claim path (services/inventory/internal/store/store.go:500-600): the ordered sequence is window -> seller -> code -> capacity, four predicates, ALL of them keyed on channel_allocations and NONE on catalog.channels. The test must reach the INSERT, so its fixture must satisfy all four -- an active allocation for the code, open window, sold_by admitting the caller (or unbound), requires_code false, cap >= qty. A fixture that fails any earlier predicate proves nothing about the registry, which is precisely how this test could be green and vacuous.

first_slice.note: DECIDED: smoke/, not the gateway suite -- there is no separate 'gateway suite'. smoke/ IS the gateway-level tier (module ticketing/smoke, black-box HTTP against the running compose stack via SMOKE_GATEWAY_URL), and it is already in make check (Makefile:20 -> :122). One new file, both halves (A and B) plus the enabled=false variant, fits one slice.

success.note: COS restated to what the code permits -- see the readiness comment. Three assertions: unregistered code sells on the public path (order verbatim); unregistered code sells on the partner path (claim AND order verbatim); a registry row with enabled=false sells identically on both. Each names the invariant in its comment and cites ADR-024.
